summary: Today presents a legal and market-focused mix, driven primarily by High Court rulings on worker retrenchment compensation and interfaith marriage law alongside Karnataka's regulatory response to Supreme Court bike taxi directions. On the business front, major strategic moves by Reliance in satellite telecom and milestone revenue contributions from U.S. Polo Assn. highlight expanding corporate footprints in India.

bullets.text: The Bombay High Court directed Bosch to pay ₹25 lakh each to retrenched workers after ruling that internal transfers were used as disguised dismissals.
The Madras High Court held that an interfaith marriage between a Hindu and a Christian cannot legally be registered under the Hindu Marriage Act.
Karnataka's transport minister is consulting the Advocate General to frame bike taxi regulations instead of a blanket ban following Supreme Court directions.
Reliance is developing a 1,600-satellite constellation network to challenge Starlink in providing satellite broadband services across India.
U.S. Polo Assn. reported that its Indian business unit now contributes 20% of the brand's total global revenue.
